images.title: HCF by minimum counts
images.purpose: Recap the minimum count method for the HCF in three short steps, using 36, 60 and 84.
images.composition: Three numbered panels in one row joined by two grey arrows, a short heading line above them, each panel holding only a line or a few tiles, with generous space around.
exact_structure: Heading line above the panels, centred: 36, 60, 84.
Panel 1 (teal #0072B2 border), heading 1 Primes in all: two teal tiles reading 2 and 3, then two grey #6B7280 tiles reading 5 and 7, each crossed out with one grey diagonal line.
Panel 2 (amber #E69F00 border), heading 2 Smallest count: the single line 2 twice, 3 once.
Panel 3 (reddish purple #CC79A7 border), heading 3 Multiply: the single line HCF = 2 × 2 × 3 = 12.
Exactly 2 grey #6B7280 arrows: panel 1 to panel 2, panel 2 to panel 3.
rejection: the 5 or 7 tile shown without a cross, or the 2 or 3 tile crossed out
images.takeaway: Keep the primes every number has, take each the smallest number of times, then multiply.
images.description: Three panels for 36, 60 and 84: keep primes 2 and 3 and strike out 5 and 7, take 2 twice and 3 once, and HCF = 2 × 2 × 3 = 12.
images.context: Shown beside the practice questions on finding the HCF by minimum counts.
images.teaching_notes: Follow the three panels in order for each practice set; a prime missing from even one number is crossed out in step 1.

image_decisions.why: A compact three step recap supports the minimum count practice.
